# E5 — is the GPU working, or waiting to be given work?

**Generated by `bench/make_e5_report.py` from the committed `timeline_summary.csv` files.** Nothing here is typed in.

A phase can be slow for three different reasons and only one of them is a memory problem. E5 separates the third: time when the GPU has **nothing queued**, because the host has not yet launched the next kernel. That time is invisible to `ncu` — which profiles kernels, and an idle GPU runs none — so it cannot be found in Part C's data at any resolution.

**Read `gpu_idle_frac_corrected` where it exists.** nsys's own tracing stretches each region by roughly ×1.53 on this device, so the raw fraction overstates idleness. Both are shown.

## Did the per-region split survive this capture?

A capture taken through `--compile-mode` has no NVTX regions: the context managers graph-break the model, so it runs `--no-regions` and reports one `whole_capture` row. A capture taken through a ladder `--rung` keeps its regions, because the rungs compile `embed_image`, `container.forward` and `denoise_step` individually and the instrumentation goes on afterwards. A single-row run below means the first thing happened — not that the phases had no kernels.

| run | regions reported | phase rows | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `20260922_E5_pi0_eager_N10` | 5 | 4 | per-region split intact |
| `20260922_E5_pi0_eager_N4` | 5 | 4 | per-region split intact |

## What this means for a memory-side accelerator

The idle fraction is the share of the phase during which **no kernel is running at all**. Whatever a memory-side design does to the kernels, it cannot touch that share — the work is not on the GPU during it. So the idle fraction is a ceiling on what any such design can remove, and it belongs next to every speedup claim in this study.

| model | mode | region | idle frac (corrected where available) | ceiling on any kernel-side speedup |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| π0 | `eager` | ae_step (denoising step) | 0.842 | 6.32× if every kernel became free |
| π0 | `eager` | whole_capture (inference) | 0.547 | 2.21× if every kernel became free |
| π0 | `eager` | ae_step (denoising step) | 0.843 | 6.36× if every kernel became free |
| π0 | `eager` | whole_capture (inference) | 0.365 | 1.57× if every kernel became free |

The right-hand column is Amdahl's law with the idle time as the serial part: even a kernel-side change that made every kernel take **zero** time would leave the idle share untouched. For π0's eager `ae_step` — 84.3 % idle — the ceiling is 6.4×, and it is reached only in the limit of free kernels. For the whole eager inference at N=10 it is 2.2×, because the two phases that are NOT dispatch-bound make up the rest of the frame.

This is the third independent measurement pointing the same way. Part B: no optimised configuration has an action expert that dominates its frame. E7: the expert is 55.5 % of π0's latency at N=10 but 22.4 % of its above-idle energy. E5: the expert is 84 % idle, so most of that latency is not work at all. The three are measuring different things and agree.
